# Pointwise normalization fusion: correctness passes; serving speed gate fails

V30/V31 compile only pointwise completion after the unchanged grouped RMS square/mean reduction. The explicit BF16 rounding before learned-weight multiplication is retained. The compiler captures neither weights nor mutable model state; unsupported initialization retains the reference before state mutation. Default remains off.

The component test passes 49 checks over BF16/F32, six row counts through 257, four magnitude scales and noncontiguous input. V30 full-model comparison passes 1,128 checks; V31 adds ordered routing and passes 1,129. MTP generation and retained-state comparison passes 367. The V31 future-draft helper accidentally enabled compiled normalization for both future-head calls: those future-head assertions prove consistency from retained states but do not independently compare compiled versus uncompiled future execution. V32 corrects that diagnostic and adds an actual head-execution assertion; its result is separate. The V31 T0/T1 catalogue passes all 30 groups.

Seven frozen paired steady-serving development rounds ran at an 8.1 GB target, 640 expert slots, MTP off, fixed 17-token prompt and 16 greedy outputs. Each arm gets one warmup in a fresh server. Round 1 is excluded because the candidate interval swapped. The six valid pairs all retain exact IDs/text, but only three improve latency. Median paired client reduction is -0.000484996288838635, i.e. a 0.04850% latency regression. The 5% gain and 80% positive-pair gates both fail. No default activation, no substitution of generator-only timing and no claim about cold compilation, larger pools or all-hit execution. Raw outputs and exact identities follow.
